title: 工学基礎Ⅱ(再履修クラス)
subtitle: Mathematical Basics for Engineering II
keywords: Engineering and manufacturing 2.Electical & Electronic engineering 3.Mathematics for EE
educationalGoal: This subject continues from "Mathematical Basics for Engineering I" in the first semester of the first year and is the base of "Basic for of Engineers" in the second year. While learning the fundamentals of mathematics, students will establish the foundation of their thinking and learning attitude as an engineer.
advice: 1.Introduction of research fields Students will learn about the research area in the field of electrical and electronic engineering, and will learn about the research efforts in that area through some specific examples. 2. Development of mathematical skills Students will review and have trainings on differentiation (differentiation method, derivatives of commonly used functions, and application of differentiation), integration (indefinite integration, definite integration, and application of integration), and vector (vector basics, vector and plane coordinates, vector and space coordinates, scalar product, and vector product), which will be widely needed in their future.
books: A textbook written in Japanese will be used.
requiredKnowledge: This course is an introduction to the field of electrical and electronic engineering. It is important to pay close attention to the technology in which each student is interested. It is also important to review mathematics (functions and graphs, trigonometric functions, exponential functions, vectors, differential methods, integration methods, and etc.) learned in high school for future learning. It is desirable to study areas that were not taken in high school using self-study and learning support systems in our university.

activityGoals.body: To Understand the role of the Faculty of Engineering in modern society and to make your own study plan.
To understand the basics of thinking as an engineer and the attitude of learning.
To understand how to calculate vectors, derivatives, and integrals.
